subject: Simulating a dataset to test Dail-Madsen model with varying K.

messages.author: 254adfd88e5d231e
messages.subject: Simulating a dataset to test Dail-Madsen model with varying K.
parts:
Dear Unmarked gurus,

Thank you so much for all your questions and amazing help following those questions!

I am hoping to find some extra help on simulating a dataset and simulating an extended Dail-Madsen model (Hostetler and Chandler 2015).

Our original research quest is to use the extended DM model to estimate daily shorebird abundance on a migration stopover site. 
We have 10 species and 6 years in the dataset, which gives us 54 species*year combinations.
I'm testing the following global model on each species*year combination separately.

fm <-  pcountOpen(~site, ~site+week+I(week^2), ~week, ~time*tide, dynamics="constant", mixture = "ZIP", pm.umf, K=useK)

So, in this model, the initial abundance varies among 29 sites,
the recruitment (immigration of migrating birds in our case) varies by sites and peaks in the middle of migration season,
the survival (probability of staying at the site during the next occasion in our case) would decrease as the migration season progress,
and the detection probability is a function of interaction between survey time and tide level at the time.

Among 54 species*year combinations, 'the maximum number of birds detected' varies between 4 and 870.
And I'm hoping to simulate above model with varying K values to see how reliable our model is depending on the K. 

I have not done any sort of data simulation before, 
so I beg for your understanding on my utter ignorance...

I'm thinking the following example that I found from https://github.com/rbchan/unmarked/blob/master/inst/unitTests/sim.pcountOpen.r#L742
may help us...? In this simulation, I'm setting 29 sites and 49 primary periods which are the mean values from our dataset.


#################################################################
## Simulate covariate model with constant intervals

sim2 <- function(lam=c(0,1), gam=c(-1,-1), om=c(2,-1), p=c(-1,1), M=29, T=49)
{
    y <- gamma <- omega <- det <- N <- matrix(NA, M, T)
    S <- G <- matrix(NA, M, T-1)
    site <- rnorm(M)
    week <- matrix(rnorm(M*T), M, T)
    time <- matrix(rnorm(M*T, 1), M, T)
    tide <- matrix(rnorm(M*T, 1), M, T)
    lambda <- exp(lam[1] + lam[2]*site)
    gamma[] <- exp(gam[1] + gam[2]*week)
    omega[] <- plogis(om[1] + om[2]*week)
    det[] <- plogis(p[1] + p[2]*time)

    N[,1] <- rpois(M, lambda)
    for(t in 1:(T-1)) {
        S[,t] <- rbinom(M, N[,t], omega[,t])
        G[,t] <- rpois(M, gamma[,t])
        N[,t+1] <- S[,t] + G[,t]
        }
    y[] <- rbinom(M*T, N, det)
    return(list(y=y, covs=data.frame(site=site,week=week,time=time,tide=tide)))
}




nsim2 <- 20
simout2 <- matrix(NA, nsim2, 8)
colnames(simout2) <- c('lam0', 'lam1', 'gam0', 'gam1', 'om0', 'om1','p0', 'p1')
for(i in 1:nsim2) {
    cat("sim2:", i, "\n")
    lam <- c(-2, 1)
    gam <- c(-1, -1)
    om <- c(0, -1)
    p <- c(-1, 1)
    T <- 5
    sim2out <- sim2(lam, gam, om, p, T=T, M=M)
    y.sim2 <- sim2out$y
    covs <- sim2out$covs
    cn <- colnames(covs)
    siteCovs <- covs[,grep("site", cn), drop=FALSE]
    yearlySiteCovs <- list(week = covs[,grep("week", cn)])
    obsCovs <- list(time = covs[,grep("time", cn)])
    umf2 <- unmarkedFramePCO(y = y.sim2, siteCovs=siteCovs,
        yearlySiteCovs=yearlySiteCovs, obsCovs=obsCovs, numPrimary=T)
    m2 <- pcountOpen(~site, ~week+I(weeks^2), ~week, ~time, umf2,
                     K=900, se=FALSE, starts=c(lam, gam, om, p),
                     control=list(trace=TRUE, REPORT=1))
    e <- coef(m2)
    simout2[i, ] <- e
    cat("  mle =", e, "\n")
    }

#png("pcountOpenSim2.png", width=6, height=8, units="in", res=360)
par(mfrow=c(4,2))
hist(simout2[,1], xlab=expression(lambda)); abline(v=lam[1], lwd=2, col=4)
hist(simout2[,2], xlab=expression(lambda)); abline(v=lam[2], lwd=2, col=4)
hist(simout2[,3], xlab=expression(gamma)); abline(v=gam[1], lwd=2, col=4)
hist(simout2[,4], xlab=expression(gamma)); abline(v=gam[2], lwd=2, col=4)
hist(simout2[,5], xlab=expression(omega)); abline(v=om[1], lwd=2, col=4)
hist(simout2[,6], xlab=expression(omega)); abline(v=om[2], lwd=2, col=4)
hist(simout2[,7], xlab=expression(p)); abline(v=p[1], lwd=2, col=4)
hist(simout2[,8], xlab=expression(p)); abline(v=p[2], lwd=2, col=4)
dev.off()

####################################################################


My questions regarding the simulation are:

1) How I may write out the quadratic effects of (week) on the gamma terms (exp(gam[1] + gam[2]*week))?

2) Is this the right simulation to do for our question? Should I just repeat this for K= 10, 100, 400, 900?

3) How I may interpret the result?

or

4) Am I completely lost and should go back and read some text before I even try? Which text would that be?


Thank you for reading through my question, and for your insights in advance!
I would really appreciate any of your help!!


Sincerely
Eunbi

Hi Eunbi,

I would not say you are "completely lost", but I would recommend getting your hands on Marc and Andy's AHM book.  They emphasize the use of simulation for understanding these models and would get you off to a good start here.
